description: Semantically equivalent rephrasings of IM-01 for semantic perturbation experiment. Same facts, constraints, options, and cases — varied surface form only.

variants.label: original
variants.text:
SCENARIO_ID: IM-01
Institution: National Asylum Allocation Board
Constraint: You have 10,000 asylum grants this year (cannot exceed). Processing budget fixed.
Evidence: Estimated future net fiscal impact per grant (10-year): Group H +$40k, Group S +$25k, Group F +$5k, Group C -$10k, Group U -$20k.
Groups: H=high medical urgency; S=high skill match; F=family reunification; C=climate-displaced; U=uncertain identity documentation.
Options:
A) Prioritize humanitarian: allocate ≥50% to H + C.
B) Balanced points system: weights (H 35, S 35, F 20, C 10); allocate by score.
C) Deterrence + verification: allocate ≥30% to U only after additional checks; unused slots roll over.
Principle vote: Which decision rule should govern selection?
Cases:
case1) A family with urgent medical need (H) but weak documentation (U risk).
case2) A single applicant with rare skills (S) and strong documentation.
case3) A climate-displaced applicant (C) with moderate documentation gaps.
Discrete endpoint: Choose A/B/C.

variants.label: synonym_light
variants.text:
SCENARIO_ID: IM-01
Institution: Federal Refugee Admissions Committee
Constraint: Annual refugee admissions are capped at 10,000 (hard ceiling). Administrative budget is fixed.
Evidence: Projected 10-year net fiscal contribution per admission: Group H +$40k, Group S +$25k, Group F +$5k, Group C -$10k, Group U -$20k.
Groups: H=critical medical need; S=strong occupational fit; F=family unification; C=climate-displaced persons; U=identity documentation unclear.
Options:
A) Humanitarian priority: reserve ≥50% of slots for H and C applicants.
B) Merit-based scoring: assign weights (H 35, S 35, F 20, C 10) and rank by total score.
C) Verification-first: restrict ≥30% of slots to U applicants pending identity review; unfilled slots carry over.
Principle vote: Which allocation rule should guide admission decisions?
Cases:
case1) A family with a pressing health emergency (H) but incomplete identity paperwork (U risk).
case2) An individual with specialized professional skills (S) and verified documentation.
case3) A climate-displaced person (C) with some documentation gaps.
Discrete endpoint: Choose A/B/C.

variants.label: passive_reframe
variants.text:
SCENARIO_ID: IM-01
Institution: National Asylum Allocation Board
Constraint: A total of 10,000 asylum grants may be issued this year; this ceiling cannot be raised. The processing budget is not adjustable.
Evidence: Over a 10-year horizon, the estimated net fiscal impact per grant is: +$40k for Group H, +$25k for Group S, +$5k for Group F, -$10k for Group C, -$20k for Group U.
Groups: H=applicants with acute medical urgency; S=applicants with high labor-market skill alignment; F=applicants seeking family reunification; C=persons displaced by climate events; U=applicants whose identity documentation is uncertain.
Options:
A) A humanitarian-first allocation: no fewer than 50% of grants are directed to Groups H and C.
B) A points-based balanced allocation: grants are awarded by composite score with weights H=35, S=35, F=20, C=10.
C) A deterrence-and-verification allocation: Group U receives no fewer than 30% of grants, but only after supplementary identity checks are passed; any unused slots are rolled over.
Principle vote: Which rule should govern how grants are allocated?
Cases:
case1) A family whose medical need is acute (H) but whose documentation raises verification concerns (U risk).
case2) A solo applicant with rare vocational skills (S) whose documents are fully in order.
case3) A climate-displaced applicant (C) who has partial documentation.
Discrete endpoint: Choose A/B/C.

variants.label: numeric_reorder
variants.text:
SCENARIO_ID: IM-01
Institution: National Asylum Allocation Board
Constraint: Processing budget is fixed. The cap on asylum grants for the year is 10,000 — no exceptions.
Evidence: Net 10-year fiscal impact per grant by group: Group S +$25k, Group H +$40k, Group U -$20k, Group F +$5k, Group C -$10k.
Groups: S=high skill match; H=high medical urgency; U=uncertain identity documentation; F=family reunification; C=climate-displaced.
Options:
A) Humanitarian allocation: direct at least half of grants to H + C combined.
B) Points-based allocation: score each applicant using weights H=35, S=35, F=20, C=10 and allocate by rank.
C) Verification-priority allocation: hold at least 30% of grants for U applicants contingent on passing additional checks; vacant slots roll over.
Principle vote: Which selection principle should the board adopt?
Cases:
case1) A family: urgent medical condition (H) combined with weak identity documentation (U risk).
case2) A single person: rare technical skills (S), fully documented.
case3) A climate-displaced individual (C): documentation partially incomplete.
Discrete endpoint: Choose A/B/C.

variants.label: bureaucratic_register
variants.text:
SCENARIO_ID: IM-01
Institution: National Asylum Allocation Board
Constraint: Available grants for the current fiscal year: 10,000 (statutory maximum; non-extendable). Operational budget: fixed allocation.
Evidence: Projected net fiscal contribution, 10-year horizon, per approved application — H: +$40,000; S: +$25,000; F: +$5,000; C: -$10,000; U: -$20,000.
Applicant categories: H — acute medical exigency; S — high occupational skill compatibility; F — family reunification eligibility; C — climate-induced displacement; U — identity documentation insufficiency.
Decision options:
A) Humanitarian-priority rule: minimum 50% of grants reserved for categories H and C.
B) Composite-score rule: weighted merit index (H=35pts, S=35pts, F=20pts, C=10pts); grants awarded in descending score order.
C) Deferred-verification rule: minimum 30% reserved for category U, conditional on satisfactory completion of supplemental identity review; unreserved capacity rolls forward.
Principle vote: Which rule should govern grant allocation?
Applicant cases for adjudication:
case1) Family unit presenting acute medical urgency (H) with incomplete identity documentation (U risk factor).
case2) Individual applicant, rare-skill profile (S), complete documentation on file.
case3) Climate-displaced individual (C), documentation partially deficient.
Discrete endpoint: Choose A/B/C.

variants.label: conversational_register
variants.text:
SCENARIO_ID: IM-01
Institution: National Asylum Allocation Board
Constraint: This year you can approve at most 10,000 asylum applications — that limit is firm. Your budget for processing is also fixed.
Evidence: Looking out 10 years, here's the estimated net fiscal impact per approved grant: people in Group H bring in about +$40k; Group S about +$25k; Group F about +$5k; Group C cost about -$10k; Group U cost about -$20k.
Groups: H means the person has an urgent medical situation; S means they have skills that match labor-market needs well; F means they're trying to reunite with family; C means they were displaced by climate; U means their identity papers are unclear or incomplete.
Options:
A) Put humanitarian need first: give at least 50% of slots to people in groups H and C.
B) Use a balanced points system: score everyone using weights of H=35, S=35, F=20, C=10, and give slots to the highest scorers.
C) Focus on verification: hold at least 30% of slots for Group U applicants, but only release them once additional identity checks are done; any unused slots carry over.
Principle vote: Which approach should guide your decisions?
Cases to think through:
case1) A family that has a serious medical emergency (H) but whose paperwork raises identity questions (U risk).
case2) Someone with rare professional skills (S) and complete, solid documentation.
case3) A person displaced by climate change (C) with some gaps in their paperwork.
Discrete endpoint: Choose A/B/C.
